[[2024–25 NBA G League season|2025]] | team2 = →[[Memphis Hustle]] | highlights = * [[NBA All-Rookie Team|NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] ({{nbay|2023|end}}) * [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] All-Freshman Team (2023) | medal_templates = {{MedalSport|Men's basketball}} {{MedalCountry|{{bk|USA}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship]]}} {{MedalGold|[[2022 FIBA Under-18 Americas Championship|2022 Mexico]]|[[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|Team]]}} }} '''Gregory''' "'''GG'''" '''Jackson II''' (born December 17, 2004) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina Gamecocks]]. ==Early life and high school== Jackson grew up in [[Columbia, South Carolina]] and attended [[Ridge View High School]].{{cite web|first=Travis|last=Branham|title=2023 PF G.G. Jackson emergesas a high major prospect|url=https://247sports.com/Article/GG-Jackson-emerges-2023-high-major-prospect-Virginia-Tech-Georgia-Tech-South-Carolina-Washington-Syracuse-149684794/|work=[[247Sports]]|date=July 30, 2020|access-date=November 11, 2022}} As a sophomore, he averaged 15.8 points and 10 rebounds as Ridge View won the South Carolina Class 5A State Championship.{{cite web|first=Lou|last=Bezjak|title=Where SC top basketball prospects stand in recruiting|url=https://www.thestate.com/sports/high-school/article252202973.html|work=[[The State (newspaper)|The State]]|date=June 22, 2021|access-date=November 11, 2022}} Jackson was named the South Carolina Basketball Gatorade Player of the Year after averaging 22.1 points, 10.9 rebounds, and 2.3 blocks per game and leading the Blazers to a second straight state title in his junior season.{{cite web|first=Emily|last=Adams|title=How freshman star GG Jackson fits with South Carolina men's basketball|url=https://www.greenvilleonline.com/story/sports/college/usc/2022/10/12/gg-jackson-south-carolina-mens-basketball-nba-draft-prospect/69550338007/|work=[[The Greenville News]]|date=October 12, 2022|access-date=November 11, 2022}} ===Recruitment=== Jackson was rated a five-star recruit and was the consensus best collegiate prospect for the 2023 recruiting class. He initially committed to play college basketball at [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]] (UNC) shortly after the conclusion of his junior season after considering offers from [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]], [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]], [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]], and [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina]].{{cite web|first=Chapel|last=Fowler|title=5-star recruit GG Jackson commits to UNC basketball with Hubert Davis|url=https://www.fayobserver.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2022/04/27/nc-unc-basketball-recruiting-2023-gg-jackson-commits-hubert-davis/9557017002/|work=[[The Fayetteville Observer]]|date=April 27, 2022|access-date=November 11, 2022}}{{cite web|first=David|last=Cobb|title=UNC basketball recruiting: GG Jackson, five-star forward in 2023 class, commits to Tar Heels|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/unc-basketball-recruiting-gg-jackson-five-star-forward-in-2023-class-commits-to-tar-heels/|work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=April 27, 2022|access-date=November 11, 2022}} Jackson later decommitted from UNC, becoming the first player to do so since [[J. R. Smith]] in 2003.{{cite web|first=Jeff|last=Borzello|title=No. 6 prospect G.G. Jackson became the first recruit to decommit from North Carolina men's basketball program since 2003|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/34245587|website=ESPN.com|date=July 14, 2022|access-date=November 11, 2022}} He ultimately [[reclassification (education)|reclassified]] to the class of 2022 and enrolled at South Carolina.{{cite web|first=Jeff|last=Borzello|title=Former North Carolina Tar Heels basketball commit G.G. Jackson reclassifies to 2022 class, commits to South Carolina Gamecocks|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/34285534|website=ESPN.com|date=July 23, 2022|access-date=November 11, 2022}}{{cite web|first=Jeff|last=Borzello|title=Can G.G. Jackson make South Carolina men's basketball relevant again? Coaches and scouts weigh in|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/insider/story/_/id/34335399|website=ESPN.com|date=August 3, 2022|access-date=November 11, 2022}} Jackson's commitment made him the highest-ranked recruit in school history.{{cite web|first=Brendan|last=Marks|title=GG Jackson commits to South Carolina after reclassifying to Class of 2022|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3452512/2022/07/23/gg-jackson-commits-to-south-carolina-after-reclassifying-to-class-of-2022/|work=[[The Athletic]]|date=July 23, 2022|access-date=November 11, 2022}} ==College career== Jackson entered his freshman season at South Carolina as the Gamecocks' starting power forward.{{cite web|first=Michael|last=Lananna|title=GG Jackson has ‘the hardest job in all of America,’ yet he smiles through it all|url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/college/article268231507.html|work=[[Charlotte Observer]]|date=November 2, 2022|access-date=November 11, 2022}} He was named the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) Freshman of the Week for the first week of the season after averaging 15 points and nine rebounds in his first two career games.{{cite web|first=Andrew|last=Lyon|title=GG Jackson Named SEC Freshman Of The Week|url=https://www.si.com/college/southcarolina/basketball/south-carolinas-gg-jackson-named-sec-freshman-of-the-week|website=SI.com|date=November 15, 2022|access-date=November 18, 2022}} Jackson was benched after shooting 0-for-8 and scoring no points in an 85–42 loss to [[2022–23 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team|Tennessee]].{{cite web|first=Michael|last=Lananna|title=Which GG Jackson will show up for USC at Kentucky? Paris trying to push right buttons|url=https://www.islandpacket.com/sports/college/article270945712.html|work=[[The Island Packet]]|date=January 9, 2022|access-date=January 13, 2022}} In the following game he scored 16 points off the bench in a 71–68 win over [[2022–23 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]].{{cite web|first=David|last=Cloninger|title=GG Jackson rebounds from benching with 16 points in upset of Kentucky|url=https://www.postandcourier.com/sports/carolina/gg-jackson-rebounds-from-benching-with-16-points-in-upset-of-kentucky/article_2fd0e648-91dc-11ed-a4ee-bb004dc8b015.html|work=[[Post and Courier]]|date=January 12, 2022|access-date=January 12, 2022}} Jackson finished the season as the Gamecocks' leading scorer with 15.4 points per game.{{cite web|first=Michael|last=Lananna|title=Offseason primer: A closer look at Lamont Paris’ USC roster as transfer season begins|url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/college/article273144575.html|work=[[Charlotte Observer]]|date=March 15, 2023|access-date=March 16, 2023}} Following the end of the season he entered the [[2023 NBA draft]].{{cite web|title=South Carolina’s leading scorer Jackson heads to NBA draft|url=https://apnews.com/article/gg-jackson-south-carolina-nba-draft-d2cf975e36bda0e1d57ea92d1bb5cdef|website=APNews.com|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|date=March 24, 2023|access-date=March 24, 2023}} ==Professional career== Jackson was selected by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] with the 45th overall pick in the second round of the [[2023 NBA draft]],{{cite web|first=Michael|last=Lananna|title=South Carolina’s GG Jackson slides in NBA Draft: a long wait but ‘a huge blessing’|url=https://www.thestate.com/sports/college/university-of-south-carolina/usc-mens-basketball/article276655006.html|work=[[The State (newspaper)|The State]]|date=June 23, 2023|access-date=June 23, 2023}} subsequently joining the team for the [[2023 NBA Summer League]]. On August 31, 2023, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Grizzlies, splitting time with their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Memphis Hustle]].{{cite web|title=Memphis Grizzlies sign GG Jackson II to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-sign-gg-jackson-ii-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=August 31, 2023|access-date=September 3, 2023}} Extensive injuries to the Grizzlies roster during the 2023–24 season led to the team recalling Jackson from the Hustle. On February 8, 2024, Jackson scored a then-career-high 27 points during a 118–110 loss to the [[Chicago Bulls]], which led to the Grizzlies signing Jackson to a four-year contract the following day.{{cite web|title=Memphis Grizzlies sign GG Jackson II to Multi-Year Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-sign-gg-jackson-ii-to-multi-year-contract|website=NBA.com|date=February 9, 2024|access-date=February 9, 2024}}{{cite web|title=Grizzlies’ GG Jackson rewarded with standard contract after historic performance|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/grizzlies-gg-jackson-rewarded-standard-191645197.html|work=Yahoo Sports|date=February 9, 2024|access-date=March 25, 2024}} On March 10, Jackson made his starting debut for the Grizzlies against the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], where he would score 30 points in a 124–93 loss.{{cite web|first=Joseph|last=Griffin|title=GG Jackson Has Career High Night In First NBA Start|url=https://www.si.com/college/southcarolina/basketball/gg-jackson-has-career-high-night-in-first-nba-start-for-memphis-grizzlies|website=SI.com|date=March 11, 2024|access-date=March 25, 2024}} On March 20, Jackson scored 35 points with seven three-point shots made in a 137–116 loss to the [[Golden State Warriors]], becoming the youngest player in NBA history to make seven threes in a game.{{cite web | last=Hanshew | first=Zak | title=Basketball Pickups: GG Jackson continues scoring binge on Wednesday | website=NBC Sports | date=2024-03-21 | url=https://www.nbcsports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/basketball-pickups-gg-jackson-continues-scoring-binge-on-wednesday | access-date=2025-12-01}} In the regular season finale on April 14, Jackson scored a career-high 44 points and recorded 12 rebounds in a 111–126 loss to the [[Denver Nuggets]], becoming the youngest player in NBA history to record 40 points and 10 rebounds in a game.{{cite web|first=Arya|last=Chawla|title=G.G. Jackson Erupts For 44 Points In Final Game As Rookie|url=https://www.si.com/nba/draft/newsfeed/gg-jackson-44-points-history|website=SI.com|date=April 15, 2024|access-date=April 16, 2024}} His 44 points also set the record for the most points by a rookie in Grizzlies franchise history.{{cite web|first=Rexwell|last=Villas|title=GG Jackson's historic scoring outburst draws rave Grizzlies reviews|url=https://clutchpoints.com/grizzlies-news-gg-jackson-historic-scoring-outburst-draws-rave-reviews|website=ClutchPoints.com|date=April 14, 2024|access-date=April 17, 2024}} On August 27, 2024, Jackson suffered a broken right foot and underwent surgery on September 4, delaying his start to the season by at least three months.{{cite web|first=Damichael|last=Cole|title=Memphis Grizzlies' GG Jackson suffers right foot injury that will need surgery|url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/nba/grizzlies/2024/08/30/gg-jackson-injury-update-memphis-grizzlies-right-foot/75020612007/|website=CommercialAppeal.com|date=August 30,
